question: How strong is healed skin compared with the skin it replaced?
answer: Weaker, for good. A cut has about a tenth of normal strength after a week, and by three months levels off at roughly 70 to 80% of unwounded skin, rarely improving much after. Scar collagen lies in dense parallel bundles, without the woven pattern, hair follicles or sweat glands of the surrounding skin.
move: Something repaired is not the same as something restored.
source: Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 2021
reference: Kumar, Abbas & Aster, Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th edition, Elsevier, 2021
